{{Short description|Chinese mathematician and educator (1920–2019)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Xu (surname 徐)|Xu (Hsu)]]|lang=Chinese}}
[[File:Leetsch Hsu.jpg|thumb|upright|Leetsch C. Hsu in [[Glasgow]], 1950]]

'''Xu Lizhi''' ({{zh|c=徐利治|w=Hsü Li-chih}}; 23 September 1920 – 11 March 2019), better known as '''Leetsch Charles Hsu''', was a Chinese mathematician and educator. He co-founded the Department of Mathematics of [[Jilin University]] and founded the Institute of Applied Mathematics and the ''Journal of Mathematical Research with Applications'' at the [[Dalian University of Technology]]. Together with American mathematician [[Henry W. Gould]], he established the Gould–Hsu Matrix Inversion Formula in 1973.

== Early life and education==
[[File:Leetsch Hsu diploma.jpg|thumb|Hsu's diploma from [[National Southwestern Associated University]]]]
Hsu was born on 23 September 1920 in [[Zhangjiagang]], [[Jiangsu]], Republic of China. His original name was '''Xu Quanyong''' ({{lang|zh|徐泉涌}}).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.tsinghua.org.cn/publish/alumni/4000351/12840201.html|title=西南联大校友、著名数学家徐利治先生去世|date=2019-03-12|website=Tsinghua University|access-date=2019-04-02|archive-date=2019-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402181602/http://www.tsinghua.org.cn/publish/alumni/4000351/12840201.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hsu studied at Jiangsu Provincial Luoshe Normal School before the outbreak of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]]. In 1940, he passed the entrance examination for the temporary [[National Southwestern Associated University]] formed by [[Tsinghua University|Tsinghua]] and other universities in [[Kunming]], and studied mathematics under [[Hua Luogeng]] and [[Pao-Lu Hsu]]. Upon graduation in 1945, he was hired by the university as a teaching assistant to Hua.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
[[File:Leetsch Hsu Tsinghua ID.jpg|thumb|Hsu's faculty ID issued by [[Tsinghua University]]]]
After the end of the Sino-Japanese War, National Southwestern Associated University was disbanded in 1946 and Hsu joined [[Tsinghua University]], which had been reestablished in [[Beijing]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1949, Hsu was awarded a scholarship by the [[British Council]] for a two-year study in the United Kingdom. He spent the first year at the [[University of Aberdeen]] and the second at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sohu.com/a/300651667_349574|title=深切缅怀我国著名数学家、教育家徐利治先生！|date=2019-03-12|website=Sohu|access-date=2019-04-02}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In 1951, Hsu returned to China and became an associate professor of mathematics at Tsinghua University. He also taught at [[Beijing Normal University]] on a part-time basis.<ref name=":0" /> In 1952, Hsu, together with [[Wang Xianghao]] and Jiang Zejian ({{lang|zh|江泽坚}}), moved to [[Changchun]] to help establish the Department of Mathematics at Northeast People's University (later renamed as [[Jilin University]]). He served as deputy chair of the department. He was promoted to full professor in 1956, and founded the study of [[computational mathematics]] at the university.<ref name=":0" />

In 1980, Hsu moved to the [[Dalian University of Technology]], where he founded the Institute of Applied Mathematics. He also established the ''Journal of Mathematical Research and Exposition'' (later renamed as ''Journal of Mathematical Research with Applications'' 数学研究及应用) and served as its chief editor.<ref name=":1" /> He also served as Chair of the Mathematics Department of the [[Huazhong University of Science and Technology]].<ref name=":0" /> From 1986 to 1987, he taught as a visiting professor at the [[Texas A&M University]] in the United States.<ref name=":0" /> He was named Honorary Dean of the School of Science of the [[Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chinanews.com/gn/2019/03-12/8778377.shtml|title=中国著名数学家、教育家徐利治因病逝世|date=2019-03-12|website=China News|access-date=2019-04-02}}</ref> In 2009, he was named by the Dalian University of Technology as one of the most important faculty members in the history of the university.<ref name=":1" />

== Contributions ==
Hsu made significant contributions to [[asymptotic analysis]], [[approximation theory]], and [[combinatorics]].<ref name=":0" /> He began collaborating with American mathematician [[Henry W. Gould]] in 1965, years before US President [[Richard Nixon]] established official relations with the People's Republic of China.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.wvu.edu/~gould/vita.html|title=Biographical Sketch of Henry W. Gould|date=2016-10-23|website=West Virginia University|access-date=2019-04-03}}</ref> Their collaboration resulted in the establishment of the Gould–Hsu Matrix Inversion Formula in 1973, which is important for computing combinatorial identities.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://jmre.dlut.edu.cn/en/ch/reader/create_pdf.aspx?file_no=20120204&year_id=2012&quarter_id=2&falg=1 |title=Gould-Hsu Inversion Chains and Their Applications |last1=Liu |first1=Hongmei |last2=Ding |first2=Shuyan |last3=Qi |first3=Shuhua |date=March 2012 |doi=10.3770/j.issn:2095-2651.2012.02.004 |journal=Journal of Mathematical Research with Applications |volume=32 |issue=2 |pages=167–173 |access-date=2019-04-03}}</ref><ref name="Weisstein2002">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=D_XKBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA1217|title=CRC Concise Encyclopedia of Mathematics|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|date=2002|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4200-3522-3|pages=1217}}</ref><ref name="LiuChai2011">{{cite book|last1=Liu|first1=Baoxiang|last2=Chai|first2=Chunlai|title=Information Computing and Application |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=da1v0C2TyakC&pg=PA145|date=2011|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-642-25254-9|page=145}}</ref>

Hsu published over 170 research papers and more than 10 [[monographs]]. He advised 20 doctoral students. and won multiple national and international prizes.<ref name=":1" />

== Death ==
Hsu died in Beijing on 11 March 2019, at the age of 98.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
